newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Aer Lingus says to buy transatlantic aircraft.
newsitem.headline: Aer Lingus says to buy transatlantic aircraft.

text.p: Irish national airline Aer Lingus said on Wednesday it planned to acquire an additional airbus A330 aircraft to operate extra services to the United States in 1997.
Air Lingus said in a statement that this will be the fifth A330 as part of a package of measures which the airline hopes will increase capacity by 16 percent between the U.S. and Ireland.
It said it hopes to double the frequency of flights to Chicago to six per week in the summer and add Newark, New Jersey as a new gateway in the U.S.
"The additional capacity and the introduction of Newark as a new gateway provide real opportunities to increase tourism into Ireland next year," marketing director David Bunworth said.
